Rashi on Menachot 97a:10:1.hebrew: כדתניא - דלמוצאי שבת מסדר קנים, ומגביה ראשה של חלה השניה, ונותן שלשה קנים על התחתונה: אחת מכאן, ואחת מכאן, ואחת באמצע, וכן על השנית בין לחם ללחם:
Rashi on Menachot 97a:10:1.english: As it was taught [in a Baraita] - That at the conclusion of Shabbat he arranges the rods, lifts the end of the second loaf, and places three rods upon the bottom [loaf]: one on this side, one on that side, and one in the middle; and likewise upon the second [loaf], between bread and bread.

Rashi on Menachot 97a:11:1.hebrew: ארבעה חלות - אמצעיות לכל סדר צריכות שלשה קנים תחת כל אחת ואחת, הרי י"ב קנים. והעליונה אין צריך אלא שני קנים, לפי שאין משוי עליה שיכבידנה על שלמטה הימנה:
Rashi on Menachot 97a:11:1.english: Four loaves - The middle [loaves] of each stack require three reeds under each and every one, which amounts to twelve reeds. And the top [loaf] requires only two reeds, because there is no weight upon it that would weigh it down onto the one below it.

Rashi on Menachot 97a:11:2.english: On the pure surface of the Table - And it does not become moldy.

Rashi on Menachot 97a:12:1.hebrew: בבינוניות - של ששה טפחים. ולקמן מפרש לה אמאי קרי לה בינונית: משום דאיכא דבצירא, ואיכא דטפיא:
Rashi on Menachot 97a:12:1.english: Of medium [size] - Of six handbreadths. And later [the Gemara] explains why it calls it "medium": because there is [a cubit] that is smaller, and there is [one] that is larger.

Rashi on Menachot 97a:12:2.hebrew: חוץ ממזבח הזהב - שהיה אמה על אמה. והקרן של מזבח העולה, שהיו לו לארבע פינותיו ארבע אבנים של אמה גובה ואמה על אמה עובי, ואותה אמה היתה באמה בת חמש טפחים. ולקמן מפרש: אי דגובה, אי דאורך ורוחב:
Rashi on Menachot 97a:12:2.english: Except for the golden altar - Which was a cubit by a cubit. And the horn of the burnt-offering altar, which had at its four corners four stones of a cubit in height and a cubit by a cubit in thickness, and that cubit was [measured] with a cubit of five handbreadths. And later [the Gemara] explains whether [this applies to] the height, or to the length and width.

Rashi on Menachot 97a:12:3.hebrew: היסוד והסובב - של מזבח העולה, וכולהו מפרש לקמן:
Rashi on Menachot 97a:12:3.english: The base and the surrounding ledge - Of the altar of the burnt offering, and all of them are explained below.

Rashi on Menachot 97a:12:4.english: The cubit of the building - Such as the wall of the Temple building and the altar of the burnt-offering.

Rashi on Menachot 97a:12:5.english: The cubit of the vessels - The Ark, the Table, and the Golden Altar.

Rashi on Menachot 97a:13:1.hebrew: (אמה וטופח - על אותה אמה תהא צריך להוסיף טפח, דהוה בת חמש, שחסירה טפח מאמה):
Rashi on Menachot 97a:13:1.english: A cubit and a handbreadth - To that cubit you will need to add a handbreadth, as it was [a cubit] of five [handbreadths], which is lacking a handbreadth from a [standard] cubit.

Rashi on Menachot 97a:13:2.english: The measurements of the altar - [This refers to] the altar of the burnt-offering.

Rashi on Menachot 97a:13:3.hebrew: באמות אמה אמה וטופח - באמות בינוניות, יהא אמה אמה וטפח דאמותיו, והן בשל חמש, דהויא לה של ששה אמה וטפח באלו:
Rashi on Menachot 97a:13:3.english: In cubits, a cubit is a cubit and a handbreadth - [Measured] in standard cubits, [each] cubit shall be a cubit and a handbreadth of its [the altar's] cubits; and they are of five [handbreadths], since [a cubit] of six [handbreadths] is a cubit and a handbreadth in these [cubits of five].

Rashi on Menachot 97a:4:1.hebrew: שולחנו של אדם מכפר - עליו, דנותן פרוסה לאורחים:
Rashi on Menachot 97a:4:1.english: A person's table atones - For him, since he gives a slice [of bread] to guests.

Rashi on Menachot 97a:5:1.english: From where are these matters [derived] - That we make supports.

Rashi on Menachot 97a:6:1.hebrew: דפוסין - שנערך ונילוש ונאפה בהן, כדאמר בריש פירקין:
Rashi on Menachot 97a:6:1.english: Molds - In which [the bread] was formed, kneaded, and baked, as it states at the beginning of our chapter.

Rashi on Menachot 97a:6:2.hebrew: קשותיו אלו סניפין - מריבוייא דקרא. לישנא אחרינא: שמקשה הלחם ומחזקו שלא ישבר, ולא מפי השמועה:
Rashi on Menachot 97a:6:2.english: “Its supports [kesotav],” these are the panels - [This is derived] from an inclusion in the verse. Another explanation: [It is called kesotav because] it makes the bread firm and strengthens it so that it will not break; and [this explanation is] not from tradition.

Rashi on Menachot 97a:6:3.english: “Its tubes,” these are the rods - For they keep the bread clear of mold.

Rashi on Menachot 97a:6:4.hebrew: שמסככין בהן את הלחם - שעל הלחם מסככין הקנים, בין חלה לחבירתה:
Rashi on Menachot 97a:6:4.english: With which they cover the bread - That the reeds form a covering over the bread, between one loaf and another.

Rashi on Menachot 97a:7:1.hebrew: לא סידור הקנים כו' - ואי ס"ד סידור קנים דאורייתא, כדמפקת לעיל:
Rashi on Menachot 97a:7:1.english: Neither the arranging of the rods, etc. - And if it enters your mind that the arrangement of the rods is by Torah law, as you derived above [why does it not override Shabbat?].

Rashi on Menachot 97a:7:2.hebrew: אמאי לא דחי שבת - דאף על גב דאין שבות במקדש, האי טלטול לאו משום שבות הוא, אלא דמיחזי כבונה וסותר:
Rashi on Menachot 97a:7:2.english: Why does it not override Shabbat - For although there is no [rabbinic prohibition of] shevut in the Temple, this moving [of the rods] is not [forbidden merely] on account of shevut, but because it appears like building and dismantling.

Rashi on Menachot 97a:8:1.english: It is possible - That Shabbat is not overridden for them.

Rashi on Menachot 97a:9:1.english: For what is the reason - He considers [the purpose of] the rods to be on account of [preventing] mold.

Rashi on Menachot 97a:9:2.hebrew: בכי האי שיעורא - ששומטן מערב שבת ערבית, ולמחר בחצי היום מסלקו ומסדר אחרים בלא קנים, ולמוצאי שבת מסדר הקנים. בכי האי שיעורא, דהוי חצי יום לזו וחצי יום לזו, לא מיעפשה:
Rashi on Menachot 97a:9:2.english: In such a period - That he slips them out on the eve of Shabbat in the evening, and on the next day at midday he removes it and arranges the other [loaves] without rods, and at the conclusion of Shabbat he arranges the rods. In such an amount of time, which is half a day for this [the old bread] and half a day for that [the new bread], it does not become moldy.

Tosafot on Menachot 97a:10:1.hebrew: לאורכו של שולחן - על הרצפה היה מניחו לאורך השולחן, דעל השולחן לא היה מקום פנוי למדוד הקנים לאורכן:
Tosafot on Menachot 97a:10:1.english: Along the length of the Table - He would place them on the floor along the length of the Table, for on the Table there was no vacant space to measure the rods along their length.

Tosafot on Menachot 97a:12:1.english: We learned there: Rabbi Meir says, etc. - This is a mishna in Tractate Kelim, in the chapter "All [Utensils of] Householders" [chapter 17].

Tosafot on Menachot 97a:13:1.hebrew: באמות אמה אמה וטופח - פירוש: מדת המזבח יהיה באותן אמות, שאמה בינונית תחזיק מהן אמה וטפח:
Tosafot on Menachot 97a:13:1.english: In cubits, a cubit [that is] a cubit and a handbreadth - Explanation: The measurement of the Altar will be in those cubits such that an ordinary cubit contains a cubit of them and a handbreadth.

Tosafot on Menachot 97a:4:1.english: His table atones for him - For great is providing a meal [to guests] (Sanhedrin 103b).

Tosafot on Menachot 97a:6:1.hebrew: קשותיו אלו סניפין - לר' יוסי קשה: מה ידרוש? כדפרישית לעיל (מנחות דף צו: ושם ד"ה לא):
Tosafot on Menachot 97a:6:1.english: “Its jars,” these are the props - According to Rabbi Yose, it is difficult: what does he expound [from this verse]? As I explained above (Menachot 96b, and there s.v. Lo).

Tosafot on Menachot 97a:7:1.hebrew: לא סידור הקנים כו' - ואף על גב דאין שבות במקדש, האי טלטול לאו משום שבות הוא, אלא משום דמיחזי כבונה וסותר, כך פירש בקונטרס. ולא משמע כן בריש כל הכלים (שבת דף קכג: ושם), דאמר: קנים קודם התרת כלים נשנו, משמע דליכא אלא איסור בעלמא. ואשכחן נמי שבות דאסרו במקדש, כגון ציר העליון שמא יתקע, נגר המונח בפ' בתרא דעירובין (דף קב. ושם):
Tosafot on Menachot 97a:7:1.english: Neither arranging the reeds, etc. - And even though rabbinic prohibitions do not apply in the Temple, this moving [of the reeds] is not on account of a rabbinic prohibition, but rather because it appears like building and dismantling - so explained Rashi. But this is not implied at the beginning of "Kol HaKelim" (Shabbat 123b and there), which states: "[The mishnah regarding] reeds was taught prior to the permitting of vessels," implying that there is only an ordinary prohibition [of handling vessels]. Moreover, we also find rabbinic prohibitions that they forbade in the Temple, such as [replacing] the upper hinge lest one drive it in, [and] a resting bolt in the last chapter of Eruvin (102a and there).
